bull_bear.body: Rs 120cr net proceeds from JFTL and wind farm divestments to be used: 60% debt reduction (Rs 200cr dollarized), 40% reinvested in aerospace/hydraulics capex; zero dividend payout policy implied; land sale to govt ensures clean capital return.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Defense order timing delays; commercial aviation recovery slower than expected; geopolitical supply chain disruptions; regulatory delays in SIPCOT NOC for JFTL sale; currency volatility on dollarized debt (mitigated by 50% export coverage); reliance on few global OEMs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, optimistic, and strategic; emphasized pricing power, operational excellence, and long-term moats; transparent about past failures (foundry) and current wins; tone reflects leadership in indigenization narrative; proactive on COVID resilience and biosecurity.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Dynamatic's UK plant captures 90%+ scrap metal value from aerospace machining by re-selling to mills — creating hidden margin; internal RTPCR testing and biosecure certification created unique customer trust during pandemic; 30-year legacy with DRDO/HAL gives unparalleled access to defense R&D pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital structure at Jun-26: Long Term debt Rs 2,994.9 mn, Short Term Rs 2,277.7 mn, Total Debt Rs 5,272.6 mn, less Cash & Cash Equivalents Rs 541.2 mn giving Net Debt Rs 4,731.4 mn; adding Lease Liabilities Rs 1,042.8 mn gives Overall Debt Rs 5,774.2 mn (vs Rs 5,554.9 mn at Jun-25).
- Net Worth strengthened to Rs 8,184.9 mn at Jun-26 from Rs 7,935.2 mn at Mar-26 and Rs 7,560.1 mn at Jun-25; LTM EBITDA Rs 2,000.1 mn at Jun-26 vs Rs 1,561.1 mn at Jun-25.
- Leverage chart shows Net Debt/Equity flat at 0.6x across Jun-25, Mar-26 and Jun-26 while Net Debt/LTM EBITDA eases from 2.8x to 2.5x to 2.4x; interest coverage (Operating Profit / Interest Expense) improves to 2.4x in Q1FY27 from 1.4x in Q1FY26 with interest expense broadly flat around Rs 140-155 mn per quarter.
- "Successful track record of enhancing manufacturing capabilities through R&D and selective acquisitions".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Hydraulics: 75% India market share in AC tractor gear pumps; expanding into hitch systems, valves (Rs 30-35k wallet); Aerospace: Sole supplier to Airbus (flap-track beams), Boeing (P-8, CH-47), Bell (fuselage); Metallurgy: German foundry integrated into aerospace supply chain; Foundry divested (JFTL) after Rs 20-25cr annual losses.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- "One of the world's largest manufacturers of hydraulic gear pumps, with over five decades of leadership in this market" and "approximately 70% share of the organized tractor market in India, supplying to nearly all major OEMs".
- "A pioneer in the Indian private sector for aerospace and defense, serving as a Tier I supplier to global OEMs such as Airbus, Boeing, Bell Helicopters, Dassault Aviation, Deutsche Aircraft, and HAL, delivering complex aerostructures, tooling, and precision parts"; the UK operation "specializes in manufacturing of high-precision airframe structures and aerospace components".
- Metallurgy "Produces intricate metallurgical ferrous castings for performance-critical components like turbochargers and exhaust manifolds, with capabilities to develop complex metallurgical components on a single-source basis", and the company "Owns one of the most advanced ferrous foundries in Europe (Germany)".
- Locational advantage: "World-class manufacturing facilities in India, the UK, and Germany strategically position our company in the post-COVID environment, as customers seek supply chain stability and prefer nearshored deliveries."
- IP moat: "Owns several patents for various products and designs in India and internationally", "Has the design IP for all the products manufactured in the Hydraulics segment", and "R&D units recognized by Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, Government of India".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [FX exposure] "The Company has exposure to EUR, GBP and USD"; on a constant currency basis Q1FY2027 revenue adjusted for a foreign exchange impact of Rs. 392.58 mn would be Rs. 3,855.5 mn, "representing an increase of 3.9% compared to an increase of 14.5% before adjustment", and EBITDA adjusted for Rs. 51.37 mn would be Rs. 499.7 mn versus Rs. 551.1 mn before adjustment.
- [Subsidiaries] Wholly owned subsidiary Dynamatic Manufacturing Limited (India) and German subsidiary Eisenwerk Erla GmbH are named; "Dynamatic Board of Directors at German subsidiary – Eisenwerk Erla GmbH" and "Casting process at the GFD molding plant".
- [Shareholding] Promoters 41.5% at Jun-26 (41.5% Mar-26, 41.9% Jun-25); FIIs 10.7%, DIIs 8.4%, Alternative Investment Fund 7.5%, Bodies Corporate 5.9%, Others 26.1%. Key investors listed include HDFC Mutual Fund, Abakkus Group, Al Mehwar Commercial Investments L.L.C. (Noosa), Alchemy and Group, Cohesion MK Best Ideas Sub-trust, Madhusudan Kela and Group and Carnelian Structural Shift Fund.
- [Governance] "Highly qualified board and management team with significant industry experience"; "5 out of 8 Directors are Independent".
- [Equity history] Year-end equity capital grew from Rs 2.9 mn at the 1974 IPO through rights issues (1987, 1992, 1994), a 1995 bonus, a 2008 amalgamation and QIP, 2014 preferential convertible warrants and QIP, to Rs 67.9 mn after a 2023 preferential allotment.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Hydraulics: 16-17% EBITDA (rising with pricing power); Aerospace: High-margin (>25% EBITDA); German metallurgy: Break-even to positive; Foundry divestment removes Rs 20-25cr annual drag; cost compression achieved via automation and digital thread efficiencies.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Aerospace revenue to rebound to pre-COVID Rs 500cr+ levels by FY23; hydraulic business to grow 20-25% CAGR over 4-5 years via wallet share expansion; defense segment to contribute 60-70% of aerospace revenue by FY24.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs 1,200+ crores (Airbus A320 family; Boeing P-8 & CH-47; HAL Tejas; Bell 407; Dassault Rafale tooling)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into UAVs (Heron, IIT Kanpur mini-drones); A350 campaign underway; potential entry into civilian drone market; leveraging German metallurgy for automotive aerospace-grade castings; defense corridor land monetization enabling capex reinvestment.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Dynamatic Technologies is a high-margin, dual-cycle aerospace and hydraulic OEM supplier with dominant market positions in Indian AC tractor hydraulics and global Airbus/Boeing aerostructures, now poised for accelerated growth due to defense indigenization, commercial aviation recovery, and wallet share expansion beyond gear pumps. The divestment of loss-making foundries and debt reduction further unlock profitability.
